claims.text: Pre-coating W particles with a thin, conformal Cu or Cu-rich layer by vapor deposition will reduce phase segregation and void formation after consolidation.
The reduced segregation and void content will improve thermal transport in the W–Cu composite.
The coated composite will preserve or enhance mechanical durability under irradiation relative to an uncoated W–Cu composite.
The initial material is a W-particle or connected-W-region composite embedded in a Cu matrix and processed by powder metallurgy such as SPS without surface modification.
Vapor deposition can be used to place a uniform nanometer-scale Cu or Cu-rich coating on W particle surfaces before sintering.
Vapor-coated W powders can be consolidated by SPS under controlled temperature, pressure, and inert-atmosphere conditions.
SPS can consolidate elemental powders into a fine-grained material with controlled structure and high density.
A continuous nanoscale Cu or Cu-rich layer on each W particle will promote intimate contact with the surrounding Cu matrix.
The interfacial coating will minimize voids and phase discontinuities.
The Cu coating enhances wettability and diffusion during sintering.
Enhanced wettability and diffusion lead to near-perfect bonding at W–Cu interfaces.
Voids and phase-separated regions impede thermal transport and compromise mechanical durability, particularly under irradiation.
Relative to an uncoated-particle baseline, the coated composite will have higher thermal conductivity.
Relative to the baseline, the coated composite will have a more uniform and defect-free microstructure.
The coated composite will maintain or improve mechanical strength and durability after irradiation.
Uncoated W–Cu composites produced by conventional powder metallurgy such as SPS are known to suffer from phase separation and void formation.
Processing is restricted to powder-metallurgy and sintering routes that do not fully melt either W or Cu.
Service testing is restricted to thermal and irradiation conditions representative of fusion-reactor divertor or joint regions.
Prior vapor-coating studies suggest that coating improves interfacial contact.
The quantitative improvement in thermal transport and irradiation-resistant mechanical durability is not yet determined.
